references.text: Our Lord God made a covenant with us at Horeb, parallel to the covenant established in Exodus 34:10.
Refers to the making of a covenant between God and Israel, the same theme as the covenant in Exodus 34:10.
Praises the Lord who does wonders (נִפְלָאוֹת), using the same word for God's wonderful works found in Exodus 34:10.
Describes God's wonderful works among the nations, linked to נִפְלָאֹת mentioned in Exodus 34:10.
You are great and do wonders, parallel to God's promise to do wonderful things in Exodus 34:10.
The Lord has done wonders (נִפְלָאוֹת), using the same language as in Exodus 34:10.
Refers to God's wonderful works in Egypt and at the Red Sea, which are examples of נִפְלָאֹת from Exodus 34:10.
Speaks of God's awesome (נוֹרָא) deeds, using the same description as in Exodus 34:10.
Describes God who has done great and awesome things (נוֹרָאֹת), linked to נוֹרָא in Exodus 34:10.
The Lord will do wonderful things among the people, fulfilling the promise in Exodus 34:10.
As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will let them see wonderful things (נִפְלָאוֹת), referring back to Exodus 34:10.
The first covenant at Sinai, which is renewed in Exodus 34:10.
Moses sealed the covenant with blood, a previous covenant act that is renewed in Exodus 34:10.
Direct allusion: Hebrews uses the Exodus covenant as a contrast to the new covenant.
Prophetic precursor: Jeremiah's new covenant is the answer to the need created by breaking the covenant in Exodus.
